content:
incident-bot: Pager: SEV2 — elevated websocket disconnects for tenant acme-corp via VPC Gateway (detected by streaming-error-rate monitor)
incident-bot: Alert details: 5m error rate 18% (baseline 0.6%), spike started ~1968007600, source: vpc-gw-prod-us-east-1, route: /streaming/connect
oncall_sre_alan: Acked — taking. Investigating routing + gateway logs :eyes:
deveng_julia: I'm seeing a pattern of 499s and 502s in the gateway logs for that tenant. Also seeing a bunch of TCP RSTs around the same time.
eng-runtime-mike: Can you paste a small snippet of the gw logs? I want to confirm whether upstream (runtime) is returning errors or the gw is cutting connections.
oncall_sre_alan:
``
2026-03-15T02:12:43Z vpc-gw-1234 acme-corp /streaming/connect 499 "client closed" src_ip=10.0.5.21
2026-03-15T02:12:44Z vpc-gw-1234 acme-corp upstream=runtime-pool-02 502 "upstream reset" latency=210ms
2026-03-15T02:12:45Z vpc-gw-1234 acme-corp tcp_rst src=10.0.5.21 dst=54.210.33.9
``
platform_sre_alan: Also saw an increase in TLS handshake timeouts on the VPC edge, likely correlated.
support_ellie: Customer says their app sees repeated websocket reconnect loops and backoff until it gives up. They're on a dedicated pool in us-east-1.
customer_ops_acme: Confirming — we started seeing errors around 02:11 UTC, our production users got disconnected and retries kept failing. We have logs showing repeated 1006 codes on our side.
eng-runtime-mike: On the runtime side, cpu/gpu metrics look fine for the dedicated pool. No OOM. But there's a spike in connection queue length on the ingress proxy that lines up with the timeframe.
deveng_julia: Is this only acme-corp? Any other tenants on same VPC gateway affected?
oncall_sre_alan: Quick check: only acme-corp's tenant id shows elevated rates. Other tenants on same gw are fine — likely tenant isolation or something with their gateway config.
pm_carlos: Could this be a client-side retry storm? If their app TTL/backoff is too aggressive when experiencing transient latency, it can amplify.
platform_sre_alan: Packet captures show many small TLS fragments and MSS path MTU differences between customer's network and our edge. Some middleboxes might be dropping fragmented frames causing TLS renegotiation and resets.
eng-runtime-mike: For immediate mitigation, options:
- Temporarily route acme-corp traffic to the alternate VPC gateway in us-west (compatible with their VPC peering) — quick failover.
- Increase edge idle/ws keepalive to reduce churn from customers with flaky networks.
- Disable request buffering on the gw for their tenant to reduce queue latency.
- Ask customer to throttle aggressive retry logic (short-term mitigation)
support_ellie: Customer prefers we handle routing change on our side — they can't push a hotfix quickly.
oncall_sre_alan: OK doing failover plan. @eng-runtime-mike can you validate fallback pool availability and any model pinning implications? We need to confirm no incompatible model versions in fallback route.
eng-runtime-mike: Checking fallback cluster... models pinned for acme are present in fallback (model v1.7 and v1.7-q8). There will be slightly higher latency (approx +40ms) but should maintain correctness.
oncall_sre_alan: Executing rollout: routing-policy update to route tenant acme-corp to vpc-gw-fallback-us-west -> applying now. Will monitor.
incident-bot: Change applied by oncall_sre_alan at 1968007805: routing change (acme-corp -> vpc-gw-fallback-us-west)
deveng_julia: I'm seeing immediate drop in 502s and RSTs from the gateway side. 499s persist but rate down to ~4%.
customer_ops_acme: We're seeing fewer disconnects now, but some clients still log transient 1006s for a short window. Thanks.
platform_sre_alan: Keep monitoring. Also opening a follow-up ticket to investigate MTU fragmentation on the peering path with acme's network team.
support_ellie: Noted. I'll coordinate with acme support to keep them updated and get their network team on a call.
pm_carlos: Also schedule a postmortem with dedicated pool owner — want to understand why tenant-only isolation occurred if others on the same gw were fine.
eng-runtime-mike: For medium-term: recommend configuring per-tenant TCP keepalive and adjust gw idle timeout to 75s for streaming tenants. Also propose a proxy tweak to reassemble TLS fragments before handing to runtime.
deveng_julia: Can we add a temporary alert on fragmented-TLS rate to catch recurrence?
oncall_sre_alan: Done. New alert rule added (frag-tls-rate) with 5m window.
incident-bot: Paging next oncall: @eng-oncall-night at 1968007920 — escalation expected in 20m if degraded recurs.
eng-oncall-night: I'll take the handoff for the night. Please leave summary + any open mitigation steps.
oncall_sre_alan: Handoff summary:
- Impact: acme-corp websocket streaming disconnects due to TLS fragment drops on VPC peering path.
- Immediate mitigation: routed tenant to fallback gateway in us-west (applied 1968007805), reduced error rate from 18% -> 4%.
- Monitoring: frag-tls-rate alert in place, logs dashboard link: https://internal.redwood/observability/dashboards/frag-tls
- Next steps: coordinate with acme network team for MTU/path fixes, implement gw TLS reassembly, adjust keepalive/idle timeout for streaming tenants.
eng-oncall-night: Got it. I'll watch overnight and escalate if >5% error rate persists for 10m.
support_ellie: Customer notified and on-call for them will follow up with network team. They appreciated the quick reroute :thumbsup: 
customer_ops_acme: Thanks team — we need a write-up for our compliance team about the outage window and actions taken.
pm_carlos: We'll produce incident summary and timeline. Assigning to me for postmortem docs.
incident-bot: Thread closed for active paging at 1968008160 by oncall_sre_alan after handoff.
